facts.raw_span: A 50-year-old man presented in 2011 for evaluation of erythrocytosis
erythrocytosis, which had been presumed to be due to polycythemia vera for the past 13 years
the patient developed dyspnea
scattered telangiectasias on the chest
Oxygen saturation of 90% to 92% with clubbing
Telangiectasias with classic spider angioma morphology on chest and back
Purple angiomatous papules on the lips resembling venous lakes
IgG κ monoclonal protein levels: 910 mg/dL
Erythropoietin levels: elevated
Intrapulmonary shunting measurements: Initial: 12.3%
Intrapulmonary shunting measurements: Later increased to: 40.5%
Intrapulmonary shunting measurements: Final measurement: 55.6%

concepts.why: The patient presents with telangiectasias, erythrocytosis, and intrapulmonary shunting, which are characteristic features of Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia.
The patient has a history of presumed polycythemia vera and presents with erythrocytosis and elevated erythropoietin levels, which are consistent with Polycythemia Vera.
The patient has elevated IgG κ monoclonal protein levels, which is a characteristic feature of Monoclonal Gammopathy.
The patient presents with oxygen saturation of 90% to 92% with clubbing, which is consistent with Hypoxia.
The patient presents with intrapulmonary shunting measurements, which is consistent with Intrapulmonary Shunting.
The patient presents with scattered telangiectasias on the chest and back, which is consistent with Telangiectasia.
The patient presents with erythrocytosis, which is consistent with Erythrocytosis.
The patient has elevated IgG κ monoclonal protein levels, which is consistent with Monoclonal Proteinemia.

rationales.F04: Telangiectasias are a hallmark of Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia.
rationales.F06: Classic spider angioma morphology is characteristic of Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia.
rationales.F08: Elevated IgG κ monoclonal protein levels are indicative of Monoclonal Gammopathy.
rationales.F11: Increased intrapulmonary shunting is consistent with Intrapulmonary Shunting and Hypoxia.
rationales.F12: Final measurement of intrapulmonary shunting further supports Intrapulmonary Shunting and Hypoxia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of scattered telangiectasias on the chest, telangiectasias with classic spider angioma morphology, and purple angiomatous papules on the lips support Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia, which explains the decisive findings without strong contradiction.
